title: The Concrete Expected-Crossing Functional, Reproduced
content: `angularIntegrand γ t` is the inner angular integral ∫_0^π |γ'ₓ(t)·sinθ + γ'_y(t)·cosθ| dθ — the per-point contribution to expected crossings, depending only on the velocity γ'(t). `expectedCrossings γ a b d` wraps it as (1/(πd)) · ∫_a^b angularIntegrand γ t dt. These are reproduced *verbatim* from the parent `BuffonsNeedleOQ01OQ01.concreteSmoothExpectedCrossings` so this file depends only on Mathlib, not on the project's internal proof chain. This is a deliberate verification choice: external checkers need only Mathlib to confirm the result.

title: Additivity Lives in the Outer Integral
content: The single-split lemma `expectedCrossings_additive` is the crux. Its proof is two steps: `simp only [expectedCrossings]` unfolds the definition, then `rw [← mul_add, integral_add_adjacent_intervals hac hcb]`. The `← mul_add` factors the shared constant 1/(πd) out of the sum, reducing the goal to additivity of the bare outer integral ∫_a^b = ∫_a^c + ∫_c^b — which is exactly `intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals`. The inner angular integral never enters the argument; neither does the geometric normalization. This is why the entry is honestly framed as a *structural* lemma rather than a deep theorem: all the mathematical content is borrowed from the interval-integral API.
mathContext: $E(\gamma,a,b,d) = E(\gamma,a,c,d) + E(\gamma,c,b,d)$ reduces, after factoring out $1/(\pi d)$, to $\int_a^b = \int_a^c + \int_c^b$. No ordering of $a, c, b$ is needed — oriented interval integrals handle the sign bookkeeping.

title: Discharging Integrability from Continuity
content: `expectedCrossings_additive_of_continuous` is the user-facing form: it replaces the two raw `IntervalIntegrable` hypotheses with a single `Continuous (angularIntegrand γ)`, the natural condition for a C¹ curve with continuous velocity. The bridge is `Continuous.intervalIntegrable`, which produces interval-integrability on any [a,b] from continuity. Providing both the raw and the continuity form mirrors standard Mathlib practice — the raw lemma is maximally general, the specialized one is convenient.
mathContext: A continuous function on $\mathbb{R}$ is interval-integrable on every compact $[a,b]$; for C¹ curves the angular integrand is continuous in $t$.

title: Noodle = Σ Needles, and a Finset/Set Membership Seam
content: `expectedCrossings_partition` is the general 'a noodle is a sum of needles' statement: for parameter points pts m ≤ … ≤ pts n, expected crossings over the whole interval equal the sum over the n−m consecutive pieces. The proof unfolds the functional, then rewrites with `sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico` and pushes the constant through with `Finset.mul_sum`. The subtlety: that Mathlib lemma quantifies its integrability hypothesis over membership in `Set.Ico m n`, but its conclusion sums over `Finset.Ico m n`. The public statement here keeps the hypothesis in terms of `Finset.Ico` (matching the visible sum), so the application must convert: `fun k hk => hint k (Finset.mem_Ico.mpr (Set.mem_Ico.mp hk))`. This one-line bridge is exactly the kind of definitional seam that hand-verification missed and machine-checking with `lake env lean` caught.
mathContext: $E(\gamma, p_m, p_n, d) = \sum_{k=m}^{n-1} E(\gamma, p_k, p_{k+1}, d)$. `Set.Ico m n` and `Finset.Ico m n` have propositionally equivalent membership ($m \le k \land k < n$) but are not definitionally equal, forcing an explicit conversion.
